title: Replicating stock with a 95-delta call and no short put
summary: A textbook synthetic long is a long call plus a short put at the same strike. The speaker instead buys a deep in-the-money call of 95 delta or more and does not sell the put, because a deep put pays very little. Without the put, delta falls from 95 toward 70 as the stock drops, which cuts exposure.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $100. Two ways to get long stock exposure for 90 days.
A: buy the $100 call and sell the $100 put. The put pays a lot at the money, so selling it makes sense here.
B: buy a $75 call of about 95 delta. A matching deep put would pay almost nothing, so the speaker skips it.
Above $100 the lines are close. Below, B loses less as its delta drops from 95 to 90, 80, 70.
B costs more up front, so its breakeven is a little higher, but its loss stops at the premium.
Risk of B: the full call premium if the stock falls below $75 at expiry.

takeaways: A long call plus a short put at the same strike replicates stock.
For a deep in-the-money call, the matching put pays little and adds a lot of downside, so do not sell it.
Without the put, falling delta reduces exposure as the stock drops.
caveats: Speech-to-text drops part of the transcript; the 95-to-70 delta path is illustrative.

scenario.label: 2018-2024: two bear markets and two rallies

backtest.note: 95-delta call as stock replacement with no short put; replaced 30 days before expiry.
